Definition: from G1909 and the base of G4476; to stitch upon, i.e. fasten with the needle:--sew on.
BiblicalUsage: Epirrhapto means to sew on, to stitch upon — and no man seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment, else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.
TheologicalSignificance: The new covenant is not sewn onto the old life, I hold: it is a new garment altogether, and the stitching proves it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
